SOFT and HARD: the two miner hardware tiers

Verification does not rest on trusted hardware. Every session must carry an activation commitment a challenger can re-check, and disputes are settled by re-execution under bond. Confidential computing is an optional upgrade, not an entry requirement.

SOFT — the default

SOFT is what a miner gets with no attested hardware inventory.

  • Any capable GPU qualifies.
  • No governed per-device ceiling.
  • Accepted capacity equals measured benchmark throughput.

What SOFT costs instead of hardware:

  • Audit exposure of about one session in forty.
  • A 1.25x surge multiplier on capacity stake while the cap is still burst-ratcheted.

HARD — specified optional tier

HARD is a specified target, not currently deployable from this repository: its attestation bridge and quote-verification transport are unbuilt. It would require NVIDIA Confidential Computing on a TDX or SEV-SNP host. In that design:

  • The measured model weights are bound to the attested environment.
  • Capacity is the lesser of measured throughput and 90% of the summed governed device ceilings.

In the HARD design, attestation failure is a 100% slash. That exposure would apply only to miners using that path once it is deployed.

Which to choose

SOFT is the current devnet development path on ordinary GPUs. Its end-to-end settlement and dispute path is still open. See Run a FLOP miner for the deployable topology and readiness checks. HARD cannot currently be selected as an operational upgrade; its governed ceiling is a cap, not a promise of higher capacity than SOFT.

Status

Draft whitepaper. The SOFT tier is ratified and first-class, but its end-to-end settlement and dispute lane is still being specified, and the currently wired settlement path remains the attested one.
